title: Positions that changed hands within a week, by the officials’ own dates
question: Where one official’s leaving statement and another’s assuming-office statement name the same position, how many days lay between them, and was the newcomer already on the payroll?
finding: 87 positions can be paired this way; the middle gap between one holder leaving and the next taking up the position is 43 days. In 35 the successor’s date is within a week of the departure or before it, and in 4 of those the successor’s name first appears on the City payroll in that same fiscal year.
how: Form 700 cover pages filed with the Ethics Commission. A leaving statement gives the date the filer left a position and an assuming-office statement the date the filer took one up. Pairs are formed where department and position wording are identical, the two filers differ, no more than four people have ever filed for that position, and the successor’s date falls between 45 days before and a year after the departure; each statement is used once, nearest dates first. Elected offices and seats on boards and commissions are left out, as are bodies that are not City departments. Listed: gaps of seven days or less (a negative gap is an overlap). The last column reads the successor’s record from the payroll by name, for names that pass the matching rules. Newcomers to the payroll come first, most recent first.
limits: Most of these are senior exempt positions, where the appointing officer may name a successor at once, often a deputy who was already acting; that is usually sensible. The form shows dates, not process: it does not say whether the position was advertised or how many candidates were considered. Position wording varies between filers, so many real successions are missed, and two people can hold like-named positions at once. Only positions that must file the form are covered.
